what: Penumbra makes the catheters and devices doctors use to pull blood clots out of arteries and veins: stroke clots in the brain, pulmonary embolisms in the lungs, and clots in the legs.
customers: Interventional neurologists, radiologists and vascular specialists in hospitals.
money: clot removal devices for brain, lung and peripheral vessels
coils and catheters for blocking vessels, plus access devices
moat: Devices designed for a procedure the company largely created, with physicians trained on its system and clinical evidence built specifically for it.
risks: 81 times earnings and 8 times sales, so the price assumes years of rapid growth
Larger device makers are entering clot removal with their own systems
Hospital capital and procedure budgets can delay adoption
opportunities: Revenue grew from $748M to $1.4B in four years with a 12.7% net margin
Clot removal in the lungs and legs is still early: most of those patients are treated with drugs today
watch: Thrombectomy revenue growth and adoption in pulmonary embolism.
